claims.text: High-temperature Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is a disordered BCC phase.
The phase stability of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a composition-driven thermodynamic instability toward chemical ordering.
Cooling Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 from its high-temperature BCC state promotes chemical short-range order and nucleation of B2-like regions.
The extent of ordering in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is controlled by diffusion kinetics during cooling or intermediate-temperature annealing.
Chemical short-range-ordered clusters precede or evolve into B2-type ordered precipitates.
The high-temperature disordered BCC state is metastable with respect to chemical ordering.
A composition-dependent deviation from ideal mixing supplies the thermodynamic driving force for local chemical ordering.
When diffusion is active during annealing, SRO clusters or embryonic B2 regions nucleate and lower the Gibbs free energy.
Rapid quenching arrests ordering and preserves a largely disordered, metastable BCC phase.
Annealing at 700°C will produce more SRO and/or B2 ordering than rapid quenching.
The annealing-induced ordering will be observable through superlattice reflections, TEM contrast, or APT-detected chemical clustering.
Changes in SRO or B2 ordering will alter hardness or yield strength.
The 600–750°C range provides significant atomic mobility while remaining below the onset of competing-phase decomposition.
At lower temperatures, frozen kinetics dominate, whereas at very high temperatures equilibrium-phase thermodynamics may dominate.
SRO can affect mechanical resistance to dislocation motion and thereby produce strengthening.
